name: journey-ceremony
comment: Agent Visibility Phase 2, Slice J1-Ceremony (re-scoped by Agent 0, 2026-08-14: verify by BEHAVIORAL/user-facing effect + the dialog completion property, never F1 identity forensics -- F1's scope=identity reads VaultBrowseDetail/VaultIdentifier catalogue-identification state, not VaultIdentity's content-addressed alias registry, and cannot see this ceremony's alias binding at all; this scenario therefore makes no vault-forensics call on purpose). Run against tests/lanista_fixtures/journeys/ceremony-use-existing-v1 (--seed, an absolute path): one confirmed Vault root holding OriginalClip.mp4 (A, PRE-REGISTERED in the seeded vault/identity.json with its real captured id/size/mtimeMs) and OriginalClipCopy.mp4 (B, a byte-identical copy whose mtime is pinned to match A's registered mtimeMs exactly). VaultLibrary::republishAtBoot() -> VaultScanner::applyPublish() -> VaultIdentity::reconcile() raises a genuine 'likely-copy' ceremony the instant the boot scan sees B match A's signature -- no scripted trigger, confirmed live during this slice's own discovery pass (identityCeremonies populated with the exact expected oldId/newId/relationship the instant vaultPage.vaultState reaches 'populated', before any click). GROUND-TRUTH CORRECTION to the plan's own assumption: VaultIdentityCeremonyDialog's Popup wrapper (objectName vaultIdentityCeremonyDialog) is NOT reachable by name through dump-ui/ui-query -- Qt Quick Controls Popups are QQuickPopup (a QObject, not a QQuickItem) and reparent their content into the window's overlay only once opened; ui-query on the wrapper name returns NO_SUCH_ITEM even while the dialog is genuinely visible on screen (confirmed live, screenshot preserved). Its CHILDREN (vaultSameMedia/vaultNewMedia/vaultUseExistingState/vaultSeparateCopy) resolve cleanly and uniquely by name with no DFS collision against Main.qml's own separate identityCeremonyDialog instance, because that instance's content is never instantiated/inserted into the overlay unless it is actually opened (never true in this journey, which never calls LocalLaunch.open) -- this scenario therefore waits on vaultUseExistingState's own visible property as the 'dialog is live' signal, never the Popup wrapper. player.sourceIdentity (J1-Video-Seam's own source-identity property) is the primary, decode-independent proof that B resolves to A's canonical identity; player.pendingSeekSec is corroborating evidence only (see fixture.json's seededResumePosition note for why 5.5s takes the player's silent-seek branch rather than the Resume/Start-Over overlay with this short a clip) -- progress-store.ini is read directly from the tagged AppData root outside the bridge (a plain file, not a bridge command) as the ground-truth store-level proof, before and after, and is not itself a scenario step.

steps.label: the session answers, drive gated on
one visible window, isolated data root
the boot splash has left the screen
open the taskbar dock
open the Vault via the taskbar folder door
the seeded fixture root paints the populated Vault
the Browse grid populates at the two-file fixture's real root count (A and B both scanned)
BASELINE: the boot-time reconcile() pass raises the ceremony automatically -- the Use Existing State affordance becomes visible with no click, the plan's own primary trigger proof
BASELINE: vaultPage's own ceremony list carries the exact expected oldId/newId/relationship (VaultIdentity's real computed values, not asserted from memory)
choose Use Existing State -- the original stable identity stays canonical, B becomes its alias

the ceremony owner's own completion property flips -- vaultPage.identityCeremonyDismissed, set true ONLY after VaultLibrary.decideIdentityCeremony() succeeds (VaultPage.qml line 1326), never an absence check
SETTLED: the ceremony list is drained, both cards remain shelved (no card removed/merged -- two distinct Browse rows survive, only their identity binding changed)
L2 verdict: both cards and the grid remain actionable and contained after the ceremony settles
open B (OriginalClipCopy) -- the newly-aliased tuple
B's detail sheet opens
click Play on B
the production player mounts for B

THE CORE PROOF: B's own player reports A's CANONICAL identity (never B's own freshly-computed id) -- progress follows the canonical identity. pendingSeekSec/decodedWidth/decodedHeight/playerReady are read as INFORMATIONAL evidence only (not gated): the seeded 5.5s resume position exceeds tiny.mp4's own real short decoded duration, so mpv.seekExact(5.5) legitimately lands at/near EOF -- PlayerPage.qml's onEndFile unconditionally clears decodedWidth/decodedHeight/fileReady exactly like an error would (the same documented race journey_play_video.json's own comment names for this identical fixture), which is a fact about the CLIP's length, not about the identity/ceremony seam this journey exists to prove. Decoded-frame readiness for a fresh local video open is J1-Video's own gated proof, not re-asserted here.
regression: back out of B (Escape -> PlayerPage.runHotkeyAction('escape') -> backRequested -> win.minimizePlayer)
regression: reopen the Vault door (was covered by the player)
regression: the Vault layer is genuinely deactivated first (a real destroy, not a hidden page)
regression: reopen the Vault (a fresh VaultPage instance, re-reading VaultLibrary/identity.json from scratch)
regression: the reopened Vault repopulates
regression: the chosen result is DURABLE across a full destroy/recreate cycle -- no ceremony re-raised (ceremonyDecisions persisted to identity.json), still 2 rows
